new_issues.description: The re-dated specification R10 is used in the abstract, introduction, §5.4, §6.1 and conclusion as the post-publication result (−0.068, p = 0.004), but it is identified under parallel trends from base year g, and the paper's own narrative is that valuations peak in exactly that year after a run-up. No pre-trend diagnostic, event-time profile, or relative-magnitude bound is reported for R10, so its significant decline is at least as trend-dependent as the headline estimate and cannot separate reversal from a coverage effect. The abstract nevertheless reports it without condition, and §5.4 ¶3 calls the absence of a positive effect 'including row R10' independent of the assumption.
new_issues.location_anchor: text: §5.4 ¶1 "When we date coverage one year after the first scored fiscal year (row R10), so that the base year is the first scored year ... the MTB effect is −0.068 (95% interval −0.116 to −0.020; p = 0.004)"
new_issues.competence_basis: R1 card: staggered DiD and event-study identification under pre-trends; the point follows from the base-year choice in Eq. (2) applied to the re-dated treatment and from Fig. 1 (MTB e = 0 is +0.017 relative to e = −1, so the run-up continues into g).
new_issues.attribution_evidence: R10 and all sentences using it are absent from original_manuscript_v1_1.md (Table 3 there ends at R9 and the heterogeneity rows); the diff adds row R10, §5.4 ¶1 and the abstract clause '−0.068 when coverage is dated one year later'.
new_issues.non_match_rationale: RR-1's committed criterion requires R10 to be reported with uncertainty and interpreted as the post-publication estimate; it does not operationalize the identifying assumption or the pre-trend diagnostics of the re-dated specification itself, which is a new analysis whose inferential status is the issue here.

new_issues.description: §4.3 explains that a p-value near 5% and a CI end near zero can disagree because the bootstrap distribution may be asymmetric. The disagreement that actually appears in Table 2 (ln total assets: CI [0.007, 0.081] excludes zero, p = 0.053) arises because the p-value is Holm-adjusted while the percentile CI is not adjusted for multiplicity. The Table 2 note does not say that the CIs are unadjusted, so the added explanation misattributes the discrepancy.
new_issues.location_anchor: text: §4.3 ¶2 "when the bootstrap distribution is asymmetric, a p-value near the 5% threshold and an interval whose end lies close to zero can therefore disagree slightly"
new_issues.competence_basis: R1 card: inference and reporting; arithmetic check that the unadjusted p for 0.044/0.018 is about 0.015–0.018 and 3 × that equals the Holm 0.053 in Table 2.
new_issues.attribution_evidence: The asymmetry sentence is new in the revised §4.3 (absent from original §2.3); the Table 2 row itself is unchanged from the original.
new_issues.non_match_rationale: RR-18 requires consistent markers and documented p-value/CI methods, which the revision provides; the issue is the correctness of a newly added explanatory sentence and the unlabelled multiplicity status of the CI column, not the marker convention.

new_issues.description: §4.2 justifies dropping the doubly robust propensity-score component because scored and never-scored firms 'overlap poorly in size'. Poor overlap is equally a problem for the outcome-regression estimator that is kept, which then extrapolates the size quadratic beyond the control support. The only support restriction (R4) trims controls from below only, and no overlap diagnostic is reported.
new_issues.location_anchor: text: §4.2 ¶2 "the doubly robust version of Sant'Anna and Zhao (2020) adds a propensity-score model, which we do not use because scored and never-scored firms overlap poorly in size"
new_issues.competence_basis: R1 card: Callaway–Sant'Anna / Sant'Anna–Zhao estimators; standard result that outcome regression extrapolates under limited overlap.
new_issues.attribution_evidence: The original §2.3 used the outcome regression without giving any reason for omitting the propensity model; the overlap rationale is added in revised §4.2.
new_issues.non_match_rationale: RR-15 concerns only how the R4 size restriction is described (lower bound only), which is fixed; it does not cover the estimator-choice rationale or overlap diagnostics.

new_issues.description: The introduction describes the pre-coverage estimate with a double negative: 'their market capitalization was −0.132 log points lower ... and their MTB ratio was −0.095 log points lower', which read literally says the outcomes were 0.132 and 0.095 log points higher. The intended meaning is 0.132/0.095 lower, or 'the estimate is −0.132'.
new_issues.location_anchor: text: §1 ¶5 "Relative to that base year, their market capitalization was −0.132 log points lower five years earlier, and their MTB ratio was −0.095 log points lower."
new_issues.competence_basis: EIC card: strict on clarity of the one headline message in a short-format paper; plain reading of the sentence.
new_issues.attribution_evidence: The original introduction stated the pre-trend as '14.1 percent' growth; the '−0.132 log points lower' phrasing first appears in revised §1 ¶5.
new_issues.non_match_rationale: RR-4 governs outcome labelling (valuation vs size), test standards and the horizon; the horizon part of this sentence is scored under RR-4, but the sign error created by the double negative is not within its criterion.

new_issues.description: Heading levels are inconsistent: Section 1 is a level-1 heading ('# 1. Introduction'), Sections 2–8 are level-2 headings, and their subsections (2.1, 3.1, ...) use the same level-2 marker as the sections, so the section/subsection hierarchy is not encoded.
new_issues.location_anchor: text: §1 heading "# 1. Introduction" versus "## 2. Related Literature and Hypotheses" and "## 2.1. Ratings, investor demand, and valuation"
new_issues.competence_basis: EIC card: exhibits and structure for a short-format journal; direct inspection of the markdown heading markers.
new_issues.attribution_evidence: Present in both versions: original has '# 1. Introduction', '## 2. Data and Research Design', '## 2.1. Sample and coverage timing'; revised keeps the same pattern. EIC-W11 mentioned it in passing, but no roadmap item carried it.
new_issues.non_match_rationale: RR-26's committed criterion covers only the Figure 1 note and the e = 4 reporting; heading hierarchy is outside it.

post_letter_observations: PLO-1 (RR-24, observed after letter reveal, agrees with 2A reading): §4.6 says simulated referee reports 'informed the revision'. 2A judged this a tool disclosure, not a reference to a review round. Keep the AI disclosure (it is required), but check that the submitted version does not imply a prior journal review round.

PLO-2 (length): the letter states that main text grew to about 7,200 words and will be shortened to the JF:IP limit before submission. A crude whitespace count of §1–§8 in the review copy (headings included, display equations excluded) gives about 8,200 words. Venue-length compliance is unverified and is a next-round check.

PLO-3 (unverifiable letter statements): 'bound documented in code (rm_bounds())', 'pre-analysis plan is in the replication package', and 'Version 2.1 adds in-text citations drawn only from the reference list already in v2; no new references were added' (v2 is not in the input set; relative to v1.1, references such as Bernama 2022, Krueger et al. 2024, Singapore Exchange 2016 are new). These cannot be checked against the manuscript and change nothing.

PLO-4 (letter references internal project records): the response letter cites 'ledger D-11' and 'ledger D-13'. A letter sent to the journal should not refer to internal ledgers; replace them with the concrete commitment.

PLO-5 (forward commitments in the letter, not yet fulfilled): (i) confirm and report the LSEG download date (RR-21); (ii) shorten the text to the JF:IP limit (PLO-2); (iii) deposit code 'upon acceptance' with a named repository (RR-16). No Schema 11 commitment_extracted lists exist, so these are advisory only.

PLO-6 (single-anonymized venue): the letter says blinded wording is used 'only in the anonymized file'. Under JF:IP single-anonymized review the submitted file carries author names; confirm which file is uploaded as the manuscript so the companion-study citation (RR-25) is the version the editor sees.

PLO-7 (routing grammar): the roadmap Sources cells ('R1-W1, R2-W1, ...') do not parse under the §10 whole-token grammar; seat labels were taken from the prefix before '-'. See the Judge Record Routing line.

PLO-8 (2A arithmetic note): the Phase 2A summary computed should_fix_addressed_rate with FULLY_ADDRESSED only (5/16). The protocol numerator counts FULLY_ADDRESSED and PARTIALLY_ADDRESSED; on 2A verdicts the rate would be 13/16 and on final verdicts it is 15/16. The 2A figure was labelled informational and is not used.
